## Real-world validation on local llama.cpp + Qwen3.6-35B MoE (AMD ROCm)

Running **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B** (hybrid GatedDeltaNet architecture) on llama.cpp with `--slot-save-path` and context checkpoints. Every turn with thinking mode produces reasoning tokens, so this bug hits on **literally every turn** of a multi-turn session.

### Symptom

`sim_best` drops significantly between turns because the empty `reasoning_content: ""` breaks the token prefix at the point where the thinking block was. llama.cpp then has to restore from an earlier checkpoint and reprocess thousands of tokens that it had already cached:

```
slot get_availabl: selected slot by LCP similarity, sim_best = 0.513  ← should be ~0.99
restored context checkpoint (pos_min = 14895, n_past = 14896)
erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 19191)
erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 23287)
erased invalidated context checkpoint (pos_min = 27383)
```

With sessions that grow to **30k+ tokens** (agentic coding with file reads), this translates to **30s–3min reprocessing per turn** that should be near-instant.

### Why the fix is in the right place

Doing this in a proxy intercept wouldn't help — the checkpoint invalidation happens because of the **token stream difference**, not the HTTP payload structure. The fix at `normalizeMessages` level is the correct layer.

### Setup

- AMD Ryzen 5 7600 · RX 7900 XT 20GB · CachyOS
- llama.cpp TurboQuant fork with ROCm/HIP + patch #22384 + #22929
- OpenCode → proxy → llama-server

Please merge this. Test coverage looks solid and the fix is minimal.

After moving a project to a new base directory and reopening it from the new location, opencode still used stale path data from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`:

- `project.worktree` still pointed to the old missing path
- one `session.directory` also pointed to the old missing path
- `project.sandboxes` already contained the new path

So opencode seems to partially detect the new location, but the UI/tool environment still relies on stale project/session paths. I saw the same pattern with another moved project too.

Manually editing SQLite is not user-friendly. It would be helpful if the UI detected missing project paths and offered a safe "Relink" / "Refresh missing project" action that preserves sessions and updates path pointers like `project.worktree` and `session.directory`.

I have also reproduced this issue on Arch Linux. Although I explicitly specified `/usr/bin/nu` as the shell in the OpenCode configuration, OpenCode still invokes `/usr/bin/bash`.

**I fixed the issue with PR #30184.**

## Root Cause

`discoverSkills` in `packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts` scans skills from five phases in fixed sequential order:

| Phase | Source | Root |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `~/.claude/skills/` | global.home + .claude |
| 2 | `~/.agents/skills/` | global.home + .agents |
| 3 | Project-level dirs | up from CWD + .opencode/ dirs |
| 4 | Config-specified paths | cfg.skills?.paths |
| 5 | Remote URLs | discovery.pull |

When the same skill basename exists in multiple roots, `Glob.scan` returns both absolute paths. Both were added to a `Set<string>`. JavaScript Set iteration order is insertion-order within a process but **not stable across sessions** — the same two paths could iterate in either order on restart. Since `state.skills` is keyed by skill **name** (not path), whichever path was processed last would overwrite the first via `state.skills[md.data.name] = {...}`. This caused `<skill><location>` to flip between `.claude` and `.agents` per session, breaking byte-level prompt cache reuse.

## Fix

### DEDUPE_MODE Design

Introduced a `DEDUPE_MODE` const object with three modes:

- **`KeepFirst`** (default): When a new basename is already in the `seen` Map, skip inserting the new path. First-discovered path wins deterministically.
- **`KeepLast`**: When a new basename is already in the Map, delete the old path from `state.matches`, then insert the new one. Latest-discovered path wins.
- **`KeepBoth`**: No deduplication — both paths remain in `state.matches`. Set iteration order determines winner (preserves pre-fix behavior).

With `KeepFirst` (default), priority across all 5 phases follows scan order:

| Priority | Source | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| Highest | `~/.claude/skills/` | Phase 1 |
| ↓ | `~/.agents/skills/` | Phase 2 |
| ↓ | `.opencode/skills/` via configDirs | Phase 3 |
| ↓ | `.claude/skills/` via upDirs (project) | Phase 3 |
| ↓ | `.agents/skills/` via upDirs (project) | Phase 3 |
| ↓ | cfg.skills?.paths custom dirs | Phase 4 |
| Lowest | remote URL pulled dirs | Phase 5 |

### Major Code Changes

**`packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts`** — `scan` function:

- Added `dedupeMode` parameter (default: `DEDUPE_MODE.KeepFirst`)
- Added `seen: Map<string, string>` to `ScanState` (basename → path)
- Deduplication logic during scan loop:

```typescript
for (const match of matches) {
  const basename = path.basename(path.dirname(match))
  const existing = state.seen.get(basename)

  if (existing !== undefined) {
    if (dedupeMode === DEDUPE_MODE.KeepBoth) {
      state.matches.add(match)
    } else if (dedupeMode === DEDUPE_MODE.KeepLast) {
      state.matches.delete(existing)
      state.matches.add(match)
      state.seen.set(basename, match)
    }
    continue  // KeepFirst: skip (first wins)
  }

  state.seen.set(basename, match)
  state.matches.add(match)
  state.dirs.add(path.dirname(match))
}
```

**`packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts`** — `discoverSkills` function:

- `state` now initialized with `seen: new Map()` alongside `matches` and `dirs`
- All 5 phase `scan()` calls pass `dedupeMode` parameter

**`packages/opencode/test/skill/skill.test.ts`** — new test block:

- `KeepFirst: deduplicates same basename from .claude and .agents, .claude wins`
- `KeepFirst: available() returns stable list across calls`
- `KeepFirst: skills with unique basenames are all retained`

## Revised: 1h TTL is now opt-in via env, defaulting to 5m

Pushed `317c1c0`, which changes the design from an unconditional `ttl: "1h"` to an env-controlled resolver that defaults to the cheaper 5-minute TTL. The new knobs are Anthropic-scoped (since `cache_control.ttl` is an Anthropic extension):

- `OPENCODE_ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` opts into the 1h TTL
- `OPENCODE_ANTHROPIC_FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` forces 5m (overrides the opt-in)
- unset -> 5m default

Applied to both the `openrouter` and `openaiCompatible` gateways. The `anthropic`-native and `bedrock` paths are unchanged.

### Why opt-in, by analogy to Claude Code

Claude Code models this exact decision with three orthogonal env vars and, crucially, makes 1h **opt-in rather than default**:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` | Request 1h TTL (opt-in) |
| `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` | Force 5m even when 1h would apply (overrides the above) |
| `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING[_OPUS/_SONNET/_HAIKU]=1` | Disable caching entirely |

Their stated reasoning ([Claude Code env-vars](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars), [How Claude Code uses prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)):

> On an API key, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS, you pay the per-token rates, so the TTL stays at the cheaper five minutes by default. To opt into the one-hour TTL, set `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`.
>
> On a Claude subscription, Claude Code requests the one-hour TTL automatically. Usage is included in your plan rather than billed per token, so the longer TTL costs you nothing extra.

The split is along the billing model: per-token paths default to 5m; only subscription paths (where 1h is plan-included and effectively free) auto-enable 1h. OpenRouter is a per-token path, so 5m-default-with-opt-in is the matching behavior.

### The cost math the previous version ignored

1h cache **writes** are billed at a higher rate than 5m writes ([Anthropic prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching), corroborated by [Cadence](https://cadence.withremote.ai/blog/prompt-caching-anthropic) and [Prism](https://ssimplifi.com/blog/anthropic-prompt-caching-explained)):

| | Write multiplier | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5m TTL | 1.25x | 0.1x |
| 1h TTL | 2.0x | 0.1x |

So 1h only pays off when a session resumes after a >5m gap but within the hour (one 1h write at 2.0x beats two consecutive 5m writes at 2 x 1.25 = 2.5x). For autonomous/walk-away runs that finish fast, or idle past the hour, the unconditional 1h premium was pure waste. See [AgentPatterns: Extended Prompt Cache TTL](https://agentpatterns.ai/context-engineering/extended-prompt-cache-ttl/) for the break-even derivation:

> Interactive review sessions are the canonical fit; autonomous loops and walk-away sessions are not. ... `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` paints every breakpoint with the 1-hour premium, including small dynamic blocks where the cost rarely pays back.

The original commit message's motivation (cache misses during review/edit/think gaps) is real and valid; this revision preserves it as an opt-in for exactly that workflow without taxing everyone else.

### How other harnesses handle it

- **aider** doesn't expose a 1h TTL at all; it keeps the cheap 5m cache warm with keepalive pings (`--cache-keepalive-pings N`), and caching itself is opt-in via `--cache-prompts` ([aider caching docs](https://aider.chat/docs/usage/caching.html)).
- **Anthropic Agent SDK / raw API** uses per-breakpoint `cache_control.ttl: "1h"` for finer control (1h blocks must precede 5m blocks in the same request).

### Tests

Reverted the assertion that expected the hardcoded `ttl: "1h"` (default is now 5m), and added two tests: one verifying the 1h opt-in lands on both gateways while leaving `anthropic`-native untouched, and one verifying force-5m overrides the opt-in. `bun test test/provider/transform.test.ts` -> 240 pass, `bun typecheck` clean.

The workaround I found was to create a custom rules markdown with the following:

````
## webfetch Tool Usage

When calling the `webfetch` tool, **never** include the `format` parameter. Omitting it defaults to `markdown`, which is the desired behavior. Only provide the `url` parameter.

**Correct:**
```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com"
}
```
````

I added this line in my opencode.jsonc to make it universal, but you could just add it to your AGENTS.md or whatever. `  "instructions": ["~/.config/opencode/custom_rules.md"],`

**Same issue on my setup — additional context:**

**Environment:**
- opencode v1.15.13 (macOS arm64, binary at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`)
- Model: Kimi K2.6 via **OpenCode Go** (`opencode-go/kimi-k2.6`, endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`)
- context-mode v1.0.160 (latest), loaded as both MCP server + plugin (`"plugin": ["context-mode"]`)
- MCP tools active: context-mode, zai-mcp-server, exa, grep, elevenlabs, context7, web-search-prime, web-reader

**Error:**
```
Error from provider: JSON Schema not supported: could not understand the instance `{'_def': {'schema': {'_def': {'type': {'_def': {'unknownKeys': 'strip', 'catchall': {'_def': {'typeName': 'ZodNever'}, '~standard': {'version': 1, 'vendor': 'zod'}}, 'typeName': 'ZodObject'}...`
```

**What I've confirmed:**
- The raw Zod v4 internal representation (`_def`, `typeName: "ZodObject"`, `~standard: {version: 1, vendor: "zod"}`) is being sent directly to the OpenCode Go endpoint without conversion to standard JSON Schema
- This happens for **all** tool schemas — built-in tools (bash, read, edit, glob, grep, etc.) AND MCP tools AND plugin tools
- Upgrading context-mode from v1.0.111 → v1.0.160 did not fix it — the issue is in opencode's core schema serialization for the Kimi provider path
- Other OpenCode Go models that use `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (MiniMax M2.7, Qwen) work fine — the issue is specific to models routed through `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` that have strict JSON Schema validation (Kimi)
- Other providers (Claude via `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, GPT, Gemini) work fine

**Config snippet** (`opencode.json`):
```json
{
  "plugin": ["context-mode"],
  "mcp": {
    "context-mode": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["context-mode"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Impact:** Kimi K2.6 is completely unusable with opencode when any tools are registered via the OpenCode Go endpoint. Would love to see #28997 or #28080 land — happy to test any fixes.
